title: Introduction to Web Development
goal: Understand how the web works and where HTML fits between the browser, the server and the other frontend languages.

topics.title: A browser turns HTML into a page
topics.body: HTML file browser ko milta hai, browser use parse karke DOM banata hai aur screen par render karta hai. Bina HTML ke page ke paas structure hi nahi hota.

topics.title: Structure, style and behaviour
topics.body: HTML structure deta hai, CSS look deta hai aur JavaScript behaviour. Teen alag responsibilities hain, isliye teen alag files me rakhi jaati hain.

topics.title: Static and dynamic pages
topics.body: Static page har visitor ko wahi HTML bhejta hai. Dynamic page server ya JavaScript se HTML badalta hai, lekin browser ko phir bhi HTML hi milta hai.

debug.title: A missing closing body tag
debug.error: Invalid document: the body is never closed, so later markup has no defined end.

debug.title: A page without a doctype
debug.error: Missing doctype: the browser falls into quirks mode and may lay the page out differently.

tasks.title: Write your first valid page
tasks.statement: Create a page with a doctype, an English lang attribute, one h1 saying `My first page` and one paragraph saying `HTML structure`.
tasks.solution:
My first page

HTML structure

interviewBank.q: What is HTML and what is it not?
interviewBank.answer: HTML is a markup language that describes the structure and meaning of content. It is not a programming language: it has no loops, variables or logic; CSS handles presentation and JavaScript handles behaviour.

interviewBank.q: How does a browser turn an HTML file into a page?
interviewBank.answer: It parses the bytes into characters, tokens and nodes, builds the DOM, combines it with CSS rules into a render tree, lays out the boxes and paints them. Scripts can change the DOM before or after painting.

defenseBank.q: A beginner says HTML is a programming language. How do you correct that gently?
defenseBank.answer: I show that HTML has no control flow or variables, then show where CSS and JavaScript fit, so the correction teaches the model instead of only naming it.
steps: Ask them what a program must be able to do.
Show that HTML only describes structure.
Show one CSS rule and one JavaScript line for contrast.

defenseBank.q: Why teach the document tree before tags?
defenseBank.answer: Once the tree is clear, nesting, indentation and closing tags stop being arbitrary rules and become the shape of the document.
steps: Draw a small page as a tree.
Map each node to a tag.
Show what happens when a branch is not closed.

mcqBank.q: Which language is responsible for the structure of a web page?
mcqBank.why: HTML describes structure and meaning; CSS styles it and JavaScript adds behaviour.

mcqBank.q: What does the browser build from the HTML document?
mcqBank.why: The document object model is the tree the browser parses and renders.

mini.title: Inspect a real page
mini.brief: Open any website, view its source and list the doctype, the title and three semantic elements it uses.
steps: Note the doctype and lang attributes.
List three structural elements and what they contain.

lab.title: Static page walkthrough
lab.brief: Write a one-page static document and explain which parts are structure, style and behaviour.
milestones: A comment marking where CSS and JS would go.

title: Setting Up Your Environment
goal: Create a project folder, write index.html and open it in a browser with working developer tools.

topics.title: A project starts with index.html
topics.body: Server aur browser dono `index.html` ko default entry point maante hain. Isliye project ka pehla file yahi naam rakha jaata hai.

topics.title: Folder structure keeps paths short
topics.body: HTML, CSS, JS aur images alag folders me rakhne se relative paths predictable rehte hain aur file dhoondhna aasan hota hai.

topics.title: Developer tools show the live DOM
topics.body: Elements panel parsed DOM dikhata hai, source file nahi. Isliye browser ke add kiye gaye nodes aur aapke file ke tags me farq ho sakta hai.

debug.title: A file saved with the wrong extension
debug.error: Wrong extension: the browser shows the file as plain text instead of parsing markup.

debug.title: A stylesheet linked from the wrong folder
debug.error: Broken path: the browser requests a file that is not there, so the styles never load.

tasks.title: Create a starter template
tasks.statement: Write a reusable starter with doctype, charset, viewport, title `Starter` and an empty body containing a comment.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Starter</title>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- page content goes here -->
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Why does the HTML file need a charset declaration?
interviewBank.answer: Without it the browser guesses the encoding and can misread non-ASCII characters. `meta charset="UTF-8"` states the encoding before the text is decoded.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between viewing source and inspecting the DOM?
interviewBank.answer: View source shows the bytes the server sent. The inspector shows the live DOM after parsing and any script changes, which is why the two can differ.

defenseBank.q: A learner cannot see their changes. What do you check first?
defenseBank.answer: I check whether they saved the file and whether the browser is loading that same file, because those two account for most "nothing happened" reports.
steps: Confirm the address bar path matches the file.

defenseBank.q: Why insist on a folder per project?
defenseBank.answer: Relative paths only stay correct when the structure is stable. A predictable layout prevents broken images and stylesheets as the project grows.

mcqBank.q: Which file name does a web server use as the default page?
mcqBank.why: index.html is the conventional directory index.

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag controls mobile layout width?
mcqBank.why: The viewport meta tag tells the browser how to scale the layout on small screens.

mini.title: Project skeleton
mini.brief: Create a folder with index.html, css/style.css and images/, and link the stylesheet from the page.
steps: Link the stylesheet with the correct relative path.

lab.title: Broken path repair
lab.brief: Take a page with two broken asset paths and repair them without moving files.
milestones: Identify both broken requests in the network panel.

title: HTML Document Structure
goal: Write every required part of an HTML document and explain what each line does.

topics.title: The doctype is not a tag
topics.body: `<!DOCTYPE html>` browser ko standards mode me chalata hai. Ye element nahi hai, isliye ise close nahi karte.

topics.title: The head describes the document
topics.body: `head` ka content page par nazar nahi aata; ye browser ko encoding, title aur metadata batata hai.

topics.title: The body is what the visitor sees
topics.body: Sirf `body` ke andar ka content render hota hai. Structure aur semantics wahin likhe jaate hain.

debug.title: A title placed in the body
debug.error: Misplaced title: the document title must live in the head, not in visible content.

debug.title: Two head elements
debug.error: Invalid structure: a document has one head, so the parser merges the stray content unpredictably.

tasks.title: Write a complete document
tasks.statement: Produce a document with doctype, lang, charset, viewport, title `Lesson 3` and a body with one h1 `Structure`.
tasks.solution: Structure

interviewBank.q: What happens if the doctype is missing?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses quirks mode, which emulates legacy layout behaviour. Box sizing and other rules can differ, so the page may look different from the standards-mode design.

interviewBank.q: Why does html need a lang attribute?
interviewBank.answer: It tells assistive technology and search engines which language the content is in, which affects pronunciation, spell-check and translation.

defenseBank.q: A learner asks why the title does not appear on the page.
defenseBank.answer: I explain the difference between document metadata and rendered content, then show the title in the browser tab so the concept becomes visible.
steps: Show the title element in the head.
Contrast it with an h1 in the body.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain the document tree without jargon?
defenseBank.answer: I draw the page as boxes inside boxes, then name parent, child and sibling on that drawing before using the terms in code.
steps: Draw html containing head and body.

mcqBank.q: Where does the visible page content belong?
mcqBank.why: Only body content is rendered in the viewport.

mcqBank.q: Which element sets the text shown in the browser tab?
mcqBank.why: The title element supplies the document title.

mini.title: Metadata card
mini.brief: Write a document whose head carries charset, viewport, title and description, and whose body carries one heading.

lab.title: Structure audit
lab.brief: Audit three pages and record which required document parts each one has or misses.
milestones: Check doctype, lang, charset, viewport and title.
Fix the page that misses the most.

title: Elements, Tags and Attributes
goal: Tell tags, elements and attributes apart, and use global attributes correctly.

topics.title: An element is a tag plus its content
topics.body: Opening tag, content aur closing tag milkar element banate hain. `img` jaise void elements ka closing tag nahi hota.
topics.code: A paragraph element

topics.title: Attributes configure an element
topics.body: Attribute name-value pair hota hai aur opening tag me likha jaata hai. `id` unique hota hai, `class` repeat ho sakti hai.

topics.title: data-* attributes carry your own data
topics.body: `data-*` custom values store karte hain jo JavaScript padh sakta hai, bina class ya id ko misuse kiye.

debug.title: An attribute value without quotes
debug.error: Unquoted value with no spaces happens to parse, but the moment the value contains a space the attribute breaks.

debug.title: A duplicated id
debug.error: Duplicate id: ids must be unique, and scripts or labels will target only the first match.

tasks.title: Annotate one element
tasks.statement: Write a paragraph with a unique id, two classes, a title and a data-role attribute.
tasks.solution: Annotated

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between an id and a class?
interviewBank.answer: An id is unique in the document and is used for fragment links and one-off targeting. A class is reusable across many elements and is the normal styling hook.

interviewBank.q: What are void elements?
interviewBank.answer: Elements that cannot have content, such as `img`, `br`, `input` and `meta`. They have no closing tag; a trailing slash is allowed but not required in HTML.

defenseBank.q: Why not use id for styling?
defenseBank.answer: An id cannot repeat, so a style tied to it cannot be reused, and specificity becomes hard to override. Classes express reusable patterns.
steps: Show two elements needing the same style.
Convert the id to a class.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain attributes to a beginner?
defenseBank.answer: I call them settings on a tag, like the size and colour chosen when buying a shirt, then show name="value" in a real tag.
steps: Remove it and show what changes.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute must be unique in a document?
mcqBank.why: Ids are unique; classes are reusable.

mcqBank.q: Which is a void element?
mcqBank.why: img has no content and no closing tag.

mini.title: Element inventory
mini.brief: Mark up a short profile using five different elements and at least three attributes.
steps: Add id, class and data-* where useful.

lab.title: Attribute repair
lab.brief: Fix a page with an unquoted attribute, a duplicate id and a class used as an id.

title: Headings, Paragraphs and Text
goal: Use headings for hierarchy and inline elements for meaning rather than appearance.

topics.title: Headings form an outline
topics.body: `h1` se `h6` tak hierarchy banati hai. Screen readers aur search engines isi outline se page ka structure samajhte hain, isliye level skip nahi karte.

topics.title: strong and em carry meaning
topics.body: `strong` importance batata hai aur `em` stress. `b` aur `i` sirf visual offset hain, isliye meaning ke liye strong/em use karo.

topics.title: pre keeps whitespace, code marks code
topics.body: `pre` whitespace aur line breaks preserve karta hai, `code` machine-readable code batata hai. Dono saath use hote hain.

debug.title: A heading level skipped for size
debug.error: Skipped heading level: the outline jumps from 1 to 4, which confuses assistive technology.

debug.title: A line break used to make a paragraph
debug.error: Layout misuse: br creates line breaks inside one block, not two paragraphs of content.

tasks.title: Mark up a course outline
tasks.statement: Write one h1, two h2 headings and a paragraph containing strong and em text.
tasks.expected:
HTML Mastery
Text
Structure
Read then practise.

interviewBank.q: Why should heading levels not be chosen by size?
interviewBank.answer: Size is a styling decision for CSS. The heading level describes the document outline, and skipping levels breaks navigation for screen-reader users and weakens SEO structure.

interviewBank.q: When is blockquote appropriate?
interviewBank.answer: For an extended quotation from another source. Short inline quotations use `q`. Neither should be used just to indent text.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses br for spacing. What do you suggest?
defenseBank.answer: I show that spacing belongs to CSS margins, while br is for meaningful line breaks such as addresses or poetry.
steps: Replace br with a margin rule.
Keep br only where the break is content.

defenseBank.q: Why teach pre and code together?
defenseBank.answer: code names the content as code; pre preserves its whitespace. Together they show a snippet exactly as written.
steps: Show it with pre and code.

mcqBank.q: Which element marks important text?
mcqBank.why: strong conveys importance; b is a visual offset without meaning.

mcqBank.q: Which element preserves spaces and line breaks?
mcqBank.why: pre keeps the source whitespace exactly.

mini.title: Article typography
mini.brief: Mark up a short article with a correct heading outline, quotes, code and an abbreviation.
steps: Write one h1 and two h2.
Add a blockquote and a code block.
Add an abbr with a title.

lab.title: Outline repair
lab.brief: Fix a page whose headings skip levels and whose paragraphs are separated by br tags.

title: Links and Navigation
goal: Build absolute, relative, internal and contact links, and make navigation usable.

topics.title: href decides the destination
topics.body: Absolute URL poora address hota hai, relative URL current file ke hisaab se resolve hota hai. Isliye project ke andar relative links rakhe jaate hain.

topics.title: Fragments jump inside a page
topics.body: `#id` same page ke element par le jaata hai. Isi se table of contents aur section navigation banti hai.
topics.code:
Skip to details

Details

topics.title: Link text must describe the destination
topics.body: Screen reader user links ki list sunte hain. "Click here" meaningless hai; "Admission form" batata hai kahan jaayega.

debug.title: A new tab opened without rel
debug.error: Missing rel: the opened page can access window.opener and navigate the original tab.

debug.title: A relative link that leaves the folder
debug.error: Broken relative path: pages/about.html is resolved from the current folder and does not exist there.

tasks.title: Build a three-link navigation
tasks.statement: Create a nav with links to index.html, about.html and a mailto link, with descriptive text.
tasks.solution: Home About Email us

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between absolute and relative URLs?
interviewBank.answer: An absolute URL contains the scheme and host and works from anywhere. A relative URL is resolved against the current document’s location, which keeps a project portable.

interviewBank.q: Why is target="_blank" paired with rel="noopener"?
interviewBank.answer: The new page receives window.opener unless noopener is set, which allows reverse tabnabbing. noopener severs that reference; noreferrer also hides the referrer.

defenseBank.q: A learner reports a broken link that works on their machine.
defenseBank.answer: I compare the address bar path with the href, because a relative path that assumes a folder is the usual cause.
steps: Read the resolved URL in dev tools.
Compare it with the file system.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain link text quality?
defenseBank.answer: I have them listen to a list of links read aloud; "click here" repeated five times shows the problem immediately.
steps: List the links by text only.
Ask which destination each one names.

mcqBank.q: Which link opens the visitor’s email client?
mcqBank.why: The mailto scheme composes an email instead of navigating to a page.

mcqBank.q: What does href="#details" target?
mcqBank.why: A fragment identifier scrolls to the matching id.

mini.title: Breadcrumb navigation
mini.brief: Add a breadcrumb trail Home / Courses / HTML to three pages with correct relative links.
steps: Add a nav with the trail.

lab.title: Link audit
lab.brief: Audit a five-page site for broken relative links, vague link text and unsafe target usage.
milestones: List every link and its resolved URL.
Rewrite vague text and add rel.

title: Lists
goal: Choose ordered, unordered and description lists, and nest them correctly.

topics.title: ul for unordered, ol for ordered
topics.body: Jab order matter karta hai to `ol`, jab sirf items ka group ho to `ul`. Har item `li` ke andar hota hai.

topics.title: Nested lists go inside the parent li
topics.body: Nested list ko `li` ke andar rakhna padta hai, warna wo parent item ka part nahi banegi.

topics.title: dl pairs terms with descriptions
topics.body: Description list me `dt` term aur `dd` explanation hota hai. Ye glossary aur metadata ke liye sahi hai.

debug.title: A list item outside its list
debug.error: Orphan list items: li is only valid inside ul, ol or menu, so the structure is invalid.

debug.title: A nested list placed after the li
debug.error: Misplaced nesting: the inner list is a sibling of the item, not its child, which changes the structure.

tasks.title: Build a nested course menu
tasks.statement: Create an unordered list with two modules, each containing two lessons.
tasks.expected:
• Module 1
  • Tags
  • Attributes
• Module 2
  • Links
  • Lists

interviewBank.q: When is an ordered list the correct choice?
interviewBank.answer: When the sequence matters, such as steps, rankings or instructions. If reordering would not change the meaning, an unordered list is more accurate.

interviewBank.q: Why should navigation be a list of links?
interviewBank.answer: A list exposes the number of items and groups them for assistive technology, while each link keeps its own destination. It also degrades gracefully without CSS.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses divs for a menu. What do you suggest?
defenseBank.answer: A nav containing a ul of links gives the same layout with structure that assistive technology understands.
steps: Rebuild with nav, ul and li.
Style it the same with CSS.

defenseBank.q: How do you teach nesting?
defenseBank.answer: I show the parent li as a folder and the nested list as its contents, then indent the markup so the shape is visible.

mcqBank.q: Which element defines a description term?
mcqBank.why: dt is the term; dd is its description.

mcqBank.q: Where must a nested list be placed?
mcqBank.why: A nested list belongs to the item it describes.

mini.title: Recipe page
mini.brief: Mark up a recipe with an ordered list of steps and an unordered list of ingredients.

lab.title: Menu semantics
lab.brief: Convert a div-based menu into nav + ul + li without changing its appearance.

title: Images and Responsive Images
goal: Embed accessible images, choose formats and serve the right size to each screen.

topics.title: alt is required for meaning
topics.body: `alt` image ka text alternative hai. Informative image me description, decorative image me `alt=""` taaki screen reader use skip kare.

topics.title: figure groups an image with its caption
topics.body: `figure` image aur uski caption ko ek unit banata hai; `figcaption` caption deta hai.
topics.output:
Marks rising from 60 to 90
Term results

topics.title: srcset lets the browser choose
topics.body: `srcset` me multiple widths aur `sizes` me layout width dete hain; browser network aur screen ke hisaab se sahi file chunta hai.

debug.title: An image with no alt
debug.error: Missing alt: a screen reader announces the file name, and the image has no text alternative if it fails to load.

debug.title: Decorative image announced by the reader
debug.error: Decorative image given alt text: it adds noise for screen-reader users instead of being skipped.

tasks.title: Write an accessible figure
tasks.statement: Create a figure with an informative image, explicit width and height, and a caption.
tasks.expected:
Students walking outside the campus library
Main campus

interviewBank.q: Why set width and height on an image?
interviewBank.answer: The browser reserves space before the image loads, which prevents layout shift. CSS can still override the rendered size.

interviewBank.q: When is alt="" correct?
interviewBank.answer: When the image is purely decorative and adds no information, so assistive technology should skip it. Omitting alt entirely is different and leaves the file name to be announced.

defenseBank.q: How do you decide between alt text and a caption?
defenseBank.answer: Alt describes the image for someone who cannot see it; the caption is visible context for everyone. If the caption already carries the meaning, alt can be shorter.
steps: Write the alt for that purpose.

defenseBank.q: Why not ship one huge image for every screen?
defenseBank.answer: Mobile users pay for the bytes and the decode time. srcset lets the browser pick a smaller file when the layout does not need the large one.
steps: Measure a large image on mobile.

mcqBank.q: What should alt contain for a decorative image?
mcqBank.why: alt="" tells assistive technology to ignore the image.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute offers multiple image widths to the browser?
mcqBank.why: srcset lists candidate resources with width or density descriptors.

mini.title: Gallery page
mini.brief: Build a three-image gallery with figures, captions and correct alt text.

lab.title: Responsive image pass
lab.brief: Add srcset and sizes to a hero image and verify the browser picks a smaller file on mobile width.
milestones: Check the network panel at 400px and 1200px.

title: Tables
goal: Build accessible data tables with captions, header cells and spans.

topics.title: A table is for data, not layout
topics.body: Rows aur columns ka relationship data hota hai. Layout ke liye table use karna accessibility aur responsiveness dono todta hai.

topics.title: caption and scope explain the table
topics.body: `caption` table ka title deta hai aur `scope="col"` batata hai ki header kis column par lagta hai. Screen reader isi se cells padhta hai.

topics.title: colspan and rowspan merge cells
topics.body: `colspan` ek cell ko multiple columns me failata hai aur `rowspan` multiple rows me. Merged cells ke saath header order check karna zaroori hai.

debug.title: Data cells marked as headers
debug.error: Header row uses td: the cells are data to the parser, so the table has no accessible header.

debug.title: A merged cell without adjusting the row
debug.error: Column count mismatch: the merged header spans two columns while the body row supplies one cell.

tasks.title: Build a marksheet
tasks.statement: Create a table with a caption, two column headers and two subject rows.
tasks.expected:
Term marks
Subject | Marks
Maths | 92
Science | 88

interviewBank.q: Why is scope important on a th element?
interviewBank.answer: It tells assistive technology whether the header applies to its column or its row, so each data cell is announced with the right label.

interviewBank.q: Why should tables not be used for page layout?
interviewBank.answer: A layout table has no data relationship, so screen readers announce meaningless row and column context, and the structure cannot reflow on small screens.

defenseBank.q: A learner’s table looks fine but fails accessibility review. What do you check?
defenseBank.answer: I check for a caption, header cells with scope, and whether the visual layout depends on merged cells without matching structure.
steps: Read the table with headers only.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain colspan?
defenseBank.answer: I describe a single cell stretching across two columns, then show the header row and body row counts must still agree.
steps: Count the cells in each row.

mcqBank.q: Which element provides the table’s accessible title?
mcqBank.why: caption is the visible, accessible name of the table.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute merges cells across rows?
mcqBank.why: rowspan makes one cell occupy several rows.

mini.title: College timetable
mini.brief: Build a weekly timetable with a time column, day headers and one merged lunch row.
steps: Merge the lunch break across all days.

lab.title: Table accessibility repair
lab.brief: Fix a table that uses td headers, has no caption and mismatched merged cells.
milestones: Convert headers to th with scope.

title: Semantic HTML5
goal: Choose semantic landmarks and elements that describe the page instead of divs.

topics.title: Landmarks describe page regions
topics.body: `header`, `nav`, `main`, `aside` aur `footer` page ke regions batate hain. Screen reader user in landmarks ke beech jump kar sakta hai.
topics.output:
Site header
Main navigation
Lesson content
Copyright

topics.title: section and article are not divs
topics.body: `article` self-contained content hai, `section` ek themed group. Sirf styling ke liye div use karo, semantics ke liye nahi.

topics.title: details and summary collapse content
topics.body: `details` native disclosure widget hai; `summary` uska clickable label. JavaScript ke bina FAQ bana sakte hain.
topics.code:
What is HTML?

A markup language.
topics.output:
What is HTML? (collapsed)
A markup language. (when opened)

debug.title: Two main elements on one page
debug.error: Two main landmarks: main must be unique, so assistive technology has no single content region to jump to.

debug.title: A div used for navigation
debug.error: No nav landmark: the link group is invisible to landmark navigation.

tasks.title: Build a semantic page shell
tasks.statement: Create header, nav, main with one article, aside and footer.
tasks.expected:
BroCode
Home
Lesson
Content
Related
Footer

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between section and div?
interviewBank.answer: A section groups content around a heading and carries meaning; a div is a generic container with no semantics. If a region has no heading or purpose, div is correct.

interviewBank.q: Why is semantic HTML good for SEO?
interviewBank.answer: Search engines read the same structure assistive technology does: headings, landmarks, links and article boundaries. Meaningful markup makes that structure unambiguous.

defenseBank.q: A teammate says divs are faster. How do you respond?
defenseBank.answer: A div and a nav render the same box; the difference is meaning. The cost is none, and the accessibility benefit is real.

defenseBank.q: How do you choose article over section?
defenseBank.answer: If the content would make sense syndicated on its own, it is an article. If it only makes sense as part of the page, a section is enough.
steps: Check whether it has a heading.
Pick the element from that answer.

mcqBank.q: Which element marks the dominant content of a page?
mcqBank.why: main is the unique primary content landmark.

mcqBank.q: Which pair creates a native collapsible panel?
mcqBank.why: details supplies the disclosure and summary its label.

mini.title: Blog page shell
mini.brief: Build a semantic blog page with a header, nav, three articles and a footer.

lab.title: Div soup refactor
lab.brief: Refactor a div-only page into semantic landmarks without changing its look.
